question.value: Can radiation pressure on dust explain the observed sub-Keplerian rotation of the disc around L2 Pup, and what dust populations are compatible with the rotation curve and SED?

evidence.quote: we aim to further extend our understanding of the structure of discs surrounding evolved stars by investigating whether the sub-Keplerian motion observed in the disc around L$_{\rm 2}$ Pup could be induced by radiation pressure on the dust.

analysis_steps.goal: Find dust populations reproducing rotation curve

method.value: TORUS Monte Carlo radiation pressure, manual adjustment of a_max or dust-to-gas ratio per radial bin

evidence.quote: In this paper we locate solutions to the rotation profile manually.

key_parameters.value: 10 radial dust types, q=3.3, a_min=1 nm

evidence.quote: we use 10 different dust types that apply over discrete radial ranges

assumptions.value: Dust and gas dynamically coupled; Draine silicates; grain density 3 g cm^-3 for Stokes number

evidence.quote: The grain mass $m_d$ is computed assuming a density of $3$ g cm$^{-3}$.

validation.value: Stokes number and coupled dust-gas velocity solution

evidence.quote: We have confirmed this by directly solving for the dust and gas velocity at each radius

method.value: Chi-square on wavelengths at a given flux for points longward of 10 micron

evidence.quote: We evaluate the goodness of fit of each model using a chi-square measure for the $N$ points of the observed SED longward of $10\,\mu$m

used_for.value: Monte Carlo radiative transfer, radiation pressure force and SEDs

evidence.quote: TORUS computes the radiation pressure force using the algorithm presented by (cite: 2015MNRAS.448.3156H).
the model with $\delta=2.5\times10^{-3}$ is the only one that is consistent with all observed points longward of $10\,\mu$m within uncertainties
which yields a required replenishment rate of $3.3\times10^{-9}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$
the disc will be depleted of dust within $\sim 20\,{\rm yr}$

findings_qualitative.value: Thermal pressure gradient alone cannot explain sub-Keplerian rotation

evidence.quote: We find that the thermal pressure gradient alone cannot explain the observed rotation profile.

claims.hypothesis: Radiation pressure on dust drives the sub-Keplerian rotation
claims.experiment: TORUS radiation pressure models compared to the observed rotation curve and SED
claims.result: A family of dust populations reproduces the rotation; SED favours delta ~1-4e-3 with decreasing a_max
claims.finding: Radiation pressure is a capable and necessary mechanism

evidence.quote: Overall we conclude that radiation pressure is a capable and necessary mechanism to explain the observed rotation profile of L$_2$ Pup

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Thermal pressure gradient with hot power-law temperature; wind-like interpretation rejected

evidence.loc: 5.2 On the possibility that the circumstellar matter is more wind-like than disc-like
evidence.quote: We therefore conclude that the disc interpretation is the more applicable

limitations_admitted.value: Models simple: vertically constant dust, no full radiation hydrodynamics

evidence.quote: Our models in this paper are dynamically and geometrically quite simple

referee_caveats_inferred: Manual solution search with degenerate parameters
Fixed disc structure inherited from CO modelling

reproducibility.score_reason: Theory paper with detailed model description but manual fitting and unreleased inputs.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Models rely on TORUS and inherited literature inputs; ALMA data not reprocessed.
